Bulgarian

[edit]

Etymology

[edit]

From Proto-Slavic *nevěsta.

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • IPA(key): [nɛˈvɛstɐ]
  • Audio (Standard Bulgarian):(file)
  • Rhymes: -ɛstɐ
  • Syllabification(key): не‧ве‧ста
  • Hyphenation(key): не‧вес‧та

Noun

[edit]

неве́ста • (nevésta) f

  1. alternative form of невя́ста (nevjásta)

Declension

[edit]
Declension of неве́ста
singular plural
indefinite неве́ста
nevésta 		неве́сти
nevésti
definite неве́стата
nevéstata 		неве́стите
nevéstite

References

[edit]
  • “невеста”, in Речник на българския език [Dictionary of the Bulgarian Language] (in Bulgarian), Chitanka, 2010

Komi-Zyrian

[edit]

Etymology

[edit]

Borrowed from Russian невеста (nevesta).

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • IPA(key): /ˈɲeʋesta/, [ˈɲeʋestä]
  • Hyphenation: не‧вес‧та

Noun

[edit]

невеста • (ńevesta)

  1. bride, fiancée

Macedonian

[edit]

Etymology

[edit]

Inherited from Proto-Slavic *nevěsta.

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • IPA(key): [ˈnɛvɛsta]
  • Hyphenation: не‧вес‧та

Noun

[edit]

невеста • (nevesta) f (plural невести, relational adjective невестински, diminutive невевче)

  1. bride
  2. newlywed (wife)
  3. daughter-in-law

Declension

[edit]
Declension of невеста
singular plural
indefinite невеста (nevesta) невести (nevesti)
definite unspecified невестата (nevestata) невестите (nevestite)
definite proximal невестава (nevestava) невестиве (nevestive)
definite distal невестана (nevestana) невестине (nevestine)
vocative невесто (nevesto) невести (nevesti)

References

[edit]
  • “невеста” in Дигитален речник на македонскиот јазик (Digitalen rečnik na makedonskiot jazik) [Digital dictionary of the Macedonian language] − drmj.eu

Russian

[edit]

Alternative forms

[edit]
  • невѣ́ста (nevě́sta) — pre-1918 spelling

Etymology

[edit]

Inherited from Proto-Slavic *nevěsta.

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • IPA(key): [nʲɪˈvʲestə]
  • Audio:(file)

Noun

[edit]

неве́ста • (nevésta) f anim (genitive неве́сты, nominative plural неве́сты, genitive plural неве́ст)

  1. fiancée, bride
  2. marriageable girl

Usage notes

[edit]
  • The vocative form, неве́сто (nevésto), can occasionally be found in religious music, such as the Russian translation of Agni Parthene on Wikipedia.Wikipedia
